source: Moussaid, Helbing, Garnier, Johansson, Combe, Theraulaz (2009), Proc. R. Soc. B 276:2755-2762, doi:10.1098/rspb.2009.0405; arXiv:0908.3131, Figure 4c-d (blue bars, experiment)
how_read: The paper prints no numbers for these bars. Bar tops were measured in pixels on the arXiv PDF page 16 rendered at 400 dpi (experiments/read_fig4.py logic, values below). In each panel the frame spans 0 to 1 and the dotted line is 0.5 (frame midpoint, checked below); bar height = (frame bottom - bar top) / (2 * (frame bottom - dotted line)). Reading error about 3 px, 0.01.
paper_text: Pedestrians avoiding a static pedestrian have a slight preference for the right-hand side in our experiments, but the asymmetry is significantly more pronounced if both pedestrians are moving.
n_note: The paper gives N=148 trajectories for condition 2; no count is printed for condition 3 (about 10 trajectories per direction per 3-minute run).
